title: Fluctuation-induced magnetoresistance in graphene Hall bars at charge neutrality
authors: Anna Grigoreva, Alex Levchenko, Eleftherios Kirkinis, Anton Andreev
abstract: In the temperature interval $T\sim 50 - 100 K$, the rate of electron-electron collisions in graphene devices may exceed the momentum relaxation rate due to disorder and electron-phonon scattering. In this regime, the motion of the electron liquid may be described by the hydrodynamic equations. In the hydrodynamic approximation, at the charge neutrality point the electric current is decoupled from the hydrodynamic flow, and the conductivity of the system is equal to the intrinsic conductivity of the electron liquid, $σ_0$. It was recently shown that the coupling of charge transport and hydrodynamic flow induced by the thermal fluctuations enhances the macroscopic conductivity of the system and results in very strong positive magnetoresistance (MR) at relatively weak fields. Here we develop a quantitative theory of the fluctuation mechanism of MR at charge neutrality and obtain analytic expressions for MR in graphene Hall bars. The functional dependence of MR on the magnetic field $H$ is sensitive to the Hall bar geometry and orientation relative to the current. We also account for the effect of momentum relaxation on MR.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for fluctuation-induced magnetoresistance in graphene at charge neutrality. By treating the electron liquid hydrodynamically, the authors derive analytic expressions showing that MR results from the coupling between charge transport and thermal hydrodynamic fluctuations. The results highlight the strong dependence of this effect on the physical geometry of the graphene sample.
main_problem: The paper develops a quantitative theory to explain the fluctuation-induced magnetoresistance (MR) observed at the charge neutrality point in graphene Hall bars.
main_result: The MR is shown to arise from the coupling between charge transport and hydrodynamic flow fluctuations, yielding functional dependencies sensitive to the Hall bar geometry and magnetic field strength.
method: The analysis employs the hydrodynamic approximation, solving coupled Langevin-Navier-Stokes equations for density and velocity fluctuations in Fourier space.
model_or_system: The system is graphene, modeled as an electron liquid exhibiting hydrodynamic behavior when electron-electron collision rates exceed momentum relaxation rates. The geometry is a Hall bar of width W and length L.
key_observables: Magnetoresistance (MR), fluctuation conductivity ($\sigma_{fl}$), and the dependence of MR on the magnetic field $H$ and geometry.
important_parameters: The ratio of collision rates ($	au_{ee}^{-1} > \gamma_p$), the magnetic length ($\ell_H$), the aspect ratio ($W/L$), and the disorder strength ($\ell_G$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on the hydrodynamic regime ($	au_{ee}^{-1} > \gamma_p$) and linear response theory applied to fluctuation sources (Johnson-Nyquist noise).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the charge-density fluctuations and induced hydrodynamic flow in the Hall bar setup, showing $\sigma_{fl}(H)$ dependence on geometry and disorder.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the hydrodynamic framework and the origin of the advection term in the current, to solving the linearized fluctuation equations in Fourier space, and finally deriving asymptotic forms for $\sigma_{fl}$ in finite geometries.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of non-equilibrium, fluctuation-driven transport phenomena in a 2D Dirac material provides advanced insights into mesoscopic transport physics, relevant for understanding quantum noise effects in solid-state systems.
